To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a global reasoning approach that reasons over semantic abstractions can achieve strong results on challenging QA datasets and (2) the approach is particularly suitable for domains with limited training data and requires only a few hours of human effort to develop.

(i) we propose a new method to answer questions using a diverse set of semantic abstractions, (ii) the method is generalizable across domains, and (iii) the method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in science QA.

(i) a structured, semantic approach is a promising direction to pursue for QA, and (ii) the use of multiple abstractions is an important component in the design of a general-purpose, structured QA system.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) How can we exploit semantic abstractions to address challenging, real-world, multi-hop, and long-tail QA problems? (2) What are the best ways to represent and search over semantic abstractions?
developing a new approach to QA that is robust to the limited training data that are typically available in real-world settings.
developing general methods for exploiting semantic information to address the challenges of QA in domains that require reasoning about diverse linguistic constructs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our method achieves state-of-the-art results for science question answering, and it is the first system, as far as we know, that can reason over a wide range and variety of semantic abstractions, which is important for many domains with limited training data.
our system outperformed all prior approaches, including neural methods, on the challenging science QA task.

our system, SEMANTICALP, is a novel method for answering multiple-choice questions in a domain with limited training data, and it outperforms several state-of-the-art methods on a collection of science QA datasets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a novel method to exploit the semantic structure of a text to answer multiple choice questions.
we have developed a new approach for exploiting the semantic abstractions of text to answer complex, multiple choice questions.
we present the first approach that reasons over a variety of semantic abstractions to answer multiple choice questions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by exploiting the semantic structure and reasoning over multiple semantic abstractions, we can achieve strong performance on multiple domains with very limited training data.
, for certain QA domains, it is possible to achieve strong performance with a simple, general-purpose, and scalable approach that does not rely on large quantities of labeled data.
semantic abstractions can be a powerful tool to address a wide range of QA tasks, even in the absence of large training datasets.
